name: CTX
description: Provides Drush commands that expose site context for AI agents.
project_description:
CTX exposes a Drupal site's structure and state to AI coding assistants as a set of Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools. It registers a single MCP server (id "ctx") built on the MCP Core module, plus roughly 55 mcp_tool plugins grouped by concern: extension management, config and config-entity CRUD, content-entity CRUD and rendering, entity-type/field introspection and ER diagrams, database queries and updates, plugin- and service-registry inspection, state, queue, watchdog, cron, cache, router and site-requirements access, managed-file creation, one-time login links, and PHP eval/script escape hatches.

Rather than describing your data model to an agent by hand, you connect the agent's MCP client to the CTX server and let it query entity types, fields, bundles, configuration, database schema, routes, services and plugin definitions directly, and (in local development) mutate them. The module ships no routes, permissions or config of its own; all HTTP access is served by MCP Core's bearer-token-gated /mcp/{server} endpoint, and the tools are the module's entire surface.

CTX is explicitly a local-development tool. Its README warns against enabling it on production or any publicly accessible site, and recommends excluding it from configuration via $settings['config_exclude_modules'][] = 'ctx'. It requires PHP 8.4, Drupal core ^11.3, drupal/mcp_core and the mcp/sdk library, and (for the recommended workflow) Drush 13.7+.
